items.title: One small step, years of work
items.body: Apollo 11 landed on the Moon on July 20, 1969. Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on its surface while Michael Collins remained in lunar orbit.
items.attribution: NASA Apollo 11
items.takeaway: Break a difficult goal into carefully prepared steps.

items.title: Persistence in research
items.body: Marie Curie received the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physics jointly with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel, and the 1911 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.
items.attribution: Nobel Prize historical record
items.takeaway: Make steady progress even when recognition takes time.

items.title: A long road to change
items.body: Nelson Mandela was released from prison on February 11, 1990, after more than 27 years in captivity.
items.attribution: Nelson Mandela Foundation
items.takeaway: Choose a long-term value and take one step toward it today.

items.title: Teamwork at the summit
items.body: Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay reached the summit of Mount Everest on May 29, 1953, as part of a larger expedition.
items.attribution: Royal Geographical Society
items.takeaway: Recognize the people and preparation behind your goals.

items.title: Experiment and iteration
items.body: The Wright brothers achieved the first sustained powered flight of a heavier-than-air aircraft at Kitty Hawk on December 17, 1903.
items.attribution: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum
items.takeaway: Treat a setback as feedback for the next attempt.

items.title: The power of principled action
items.body: Rosa Parks was arrested in Montgomery, Alabama, on December 1, 1955, after refusing to surrender her bus seat to a white passenger.
items.attribution: National Park Service
items.takeaway: Choose a principle that deserves consistent action.

items.title: Work that outlasts its moment
items.body: Alan Turing helped develop foundational ideas in computing and contributed to British codebreaking during World War II.
items.attribution: The Alan Turing Institute
items.takeaway: Invest time in learning something whose value compounds.

items.title: Patience in complex projects
items.body: The James Webb Space Telescope launched on December 25, 2021, following decades of development and testing.
items.attribution: NASA Webb mission
items.takeaway: Progress can be slow and still be meaningful.

items.title: One step starts a movement
items.body: The Salt March began in March 1930, when Mohandas Gandhi led a nonviolent protest against the British salt tax.
items.attribution: Encyclopaedia Britannica
items.takeaway: Take one visible action toward a larger goal.

items.title: Careful observation
items.body: Jane Goodall began her long-term chimpanzee research at Gombe in 1960, transforming understanding of primate behavior.
items.attribution: Jane Goodall Institute
items.takeaway: Observe your habits before trying to change them.

items.title: Control the controllable
items.body: Stoic philosophy distinguishes what depends on our choices from what lies outside them.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Write two columns: what you can influence and what you cannot. Act on the first.

items.title: Respond, don't react
items.body: A pause between an event and your response can create room for considered judgment.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: When interrupted, count to five before choosing your response.

items.title: Examine your assumptions
items.body: A difficult feeling may be intensified by an interpretation rather than the event alone.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Write one alternative explanation for today's frustration.

items.title: Practice without applause
items.body: An action can express your values even when no one notices it.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Complete one useful task without seeking recognition.

items.title: Character through repetition
items.body: Virtue ethics places importance on the habits and dispositions developed through action.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Repeat one small act that reflects the person you want to become.

items.title: Choose the middle path
items.body: Practical wisdom often requires finding a proportionate response rather than an extreme.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Before acting, ask what would be too little and what would be too much.

items.title: Notice the present
items.body: Mindfulness involves attending to experience rather than automatically following every thought.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Spend two minutes observing your breath and surroundings.

items.title: Allow change
items.body: Buddhist traditions emphasize impermanence as a feature of lived experience.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Name one changing situation and adapt your plan accordingly.

items.title: Respond with compassion
items.body: Compassion can guide action without requiring that you agree with every behavior.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Offer a thoughtful response to someone having a difficult day.

items.title: Let go of certainty
items.body: Intellectual humility means leaving room for the possibility that your current belief is incomplete.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Ask one sincere question before defending your opinion.

items.title: Think in experiments
items.body: Pragmatism attends to the practical consequences of ideas and beliefs.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Try one low-risk experiment before making a big commitment.

items.title: Revise the method
items.body: A strategy is a tool, not an identity. A failed method need not invalidate your goal.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Change one part of a routine that isn't working.

items.title: Define a meaningful choice
items.body: Existentialist thought examines freedom, responsibility, and how people live their commitments.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Choose one action that reflects a value you claim to hold.

items.title: Own your decision
items.body: Responsibility becomes clearer when you acknowledge the choices available to you.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Write down a decision you can make today and its likely tradeoffs.

items.title: Respect other perspectives
items.body: Moral reasoning improves when you take another person's interests seriously.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Explain a disagreement in terms the other person would recognize.

items.title: Think beyond yourself
items.body: Ethics asks us to consider how our choices affect other people.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Before acting, identify who else may bear the consequences.

items.title: Make space for rest
items.body: A sustainable life needs more than an endless sequence of tasks.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Schedule a short period of genuine rest today.

items.title: Define enough
items.body: Well-being is not always the same as maximizing output or possessions.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Write what would count as a good-enough day.

items.title: Distinguish facts from stories
items.body: Knowing what happened differs from interpreting why it happened.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Separate three observations from your assumptions about them.

items.title: Seek disconfirming evidence
items.body: Strong beliefs become more reliable when they can survive thoughtful challenge.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Look for one credible reason your first conclusion might be wrong.

items.title: Balance courage and caution
items.body: Courage is not the absence of risk awareness; practical judgment matters.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Choose a small brave step with a sensible safety margin.

items.title: Practice fairness
items.body: Fairness asks us to evaluate comparable cases by comparable standards.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Check whether you'd judge the same action differently if someone else did it.

items.title: Listen before advising
items.body: Understanding another person's experience can be more useful than an immediate solution.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Ask what kind of help the other person wants.

items.title: Question inherited habits
items.body: Some routines survive because they are familiar, not because they still serve you.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Identify one default behavior and decide whether to keep it.

items.title: Be patient with complexity
items.body: Difficult questions may require several perspectives and more than one attempt.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Break a complicated problem into what you know and what you need to learn.

items.title: Choose deliberate attention
items.body: Attention is limited; where you direct it influences what you learn and do.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Protect one 20-minute period from interruptions.

items.title: Keep promises realistic
items.body: Integrity includes making commitments you can reasonably honor.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Renegotiate one unrealistic commitment rather than silently dropping it.

items.title: Make room for uncertainty
items.body: Not knowing is a reason to investigate, not always a reason to freeze.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: List the next piece of information that would help you decide.

items.title: Support someone else's growth
items.body: A meaningful contribution can be helping another person succeed.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Offer specific encouragement or useful feedback to a colleague.

items.title: End the day with reflection
items.body: Reflection can convert experience into a better decision tomorrow.
items.attribution: MyDayCoach original reflection — not a historical quotation
items.takeaway: Write one lesson and one adjustment before bed.
